title: We built an AI-powered IDE for game development and looking for early access testers
author: Plastic_Bag6171
selftext:
Hey all                                                                                                                                                                                                               

We've been working on EngineForge, a VS Code fork built specifically for game development.

It automatically indexes your project into a code graph, structure, dependencies, and relationships, so the AI agent has a deep understanding of your game before writing a single line. 

From there it can connect to your engine in real-time, write code, create objects and nodes, attach scripts, and manipulate scenes directly.

We're opening early access soon, and it will be **free** during the early access phase, including full AI agent usage.

Right now we're mainly looking for feedback from game developers of all experience levels, whether you've shipped games before, are working on your first project, or are just curious about AI-assisted game development.

Supported engines:

  \- Unity 2021.3+

  \- Godot 4.0+

If you're interested, you can join the waitlist or read more about how it works at [engineforge.ai](http://engineforge.ai)

comments.author: skoyrams
comments.body: does it support BYOK ( Bring your own Key) ?

replies.author: odragora
replies.body: And BYOLM (bring your own local model)

replies.author: Plastic_Bag6171
replies.body:
Not at the moment. 

We handle the AI infrastructure on our side so you don't have to manage API keys or worry about token costs during early access. 

It's something we may consider down the road based on demand.

comments.author: Melodic-Chemistry127
comments.body:
What's the main reason why someone should use your tool vs Claude Code, OpenCode etc? Is it the Engine Bridge, or are there any other killer features you are cooking?

Also, I'm one of the people who can burn $100 in Claude credits easily and I have migrated to local and open weight models, because the SOTA commercial model pricing is unsustainable for indie. You may want to consider that when thinking of your pricing, maybe consider using some sort of self hosted(your infra) open weight model, which would probably give you better margins as well.
